fields.name: echo_payload
fields.label: Echo payload (opaque)
fields.desc: duss_event_ping is a 3-instruction trampoline: it reads the incoming event struct's length field (struct offset 0x10) and data pointer (struct offset 0x14) and tail-calls duss_event_resp_data_v2(ctx, len, data) with them unchanged. It never inspects or validates the payload at all -- whatever bytes the sender puts here are echoed back verbatim as the response. Length and content are entirely sender-defined; in practice this is used to carry a counter/timestamp for round-trip-time or liveness checks, exactly like ICMP ping, but the wire format itself has no fixed fields.

name: Push Param Set
note: Checked, in order: (1) libduml_frwk.so's one built-in 6-entry dynamic-command table (duss_event_create_dynamic_cmd_tbl, vaddr 0x1098fc on E1E) -- fully dumped and decoded; its 6 entries are cmd_set/cmd_id {0x00/0x00, 0x00/0x2f, 0x00/0x89, 0x00/0xaa, 0x00/0xfa, 0x51/0x05}. None is 0x00/0x02-0x06. (2) dji_sys's direct, literal-immediate duss_event_register_dynamic_command call sites (11 total, confirmed by `blx 9bd0 <duss_event_register_dynamic_command@plt>` xrefs): 3x cmd_set 0x22/cmd_id 0x60 (Demo Mode, matches prior doc04 finding), 2x cmd_set 0x00/cmd_id 0xa3 (USB State Report, matches catalog), 2x cmd_set 0x06/cmd_id 0x3a, 1x cmd_set 0x04/cmd_id 0x69 -- none under cmd_set 0x00 match 0x02-0x06. (3) The remaining 2 of those 11 call sites (vaddr 0x2da62 and 0x70048 in dji_sys) are NOT literal-immediate: they loop over a runtime-populated table of {cmd_set, N cmd_ids, shared handler} sub-tables, reading cmd_set from a per-table field and cmd_id from array position -- architecturally exactly the shape the task describes for a generic cross-chip param bus. Traced the table pointer back to a lazily-initialized .bss global, which in turn traces to three custom ELF sections literally named `param_manager_local` (0xa8250, 56 bytes), `param_manager_buf_local` (0xa8288, 32 bytes) and `param_manager_remote` (0xa82a8, 12 bytes) in dji_sys -- strong confirmation a real 'Param Manager' subsystem exists and matches ~40 'PM:'-prefixed debug strings describing a hash-keyed named-parameter protocol with push-frequency subscriptions and remote get/set (e.g. 'PM:register remote param item err, name: %s, freq: %d', 'PM:recieved push remote param hash was not register, hash: %u', 'PM:request_remote_param_fix_send failed, freq: %d, ret: %d'). However: (a) param_manager_local on this specific image contains only one populated entry (name 'sysmode_param_block'), (b) I could not resolve which literal (cmd_set, cmd_id) values the data-driven loop registers for it (the loop itself derives them from table position/fields at runtime, not a literal I could read statically with confidence), and (c) repeated attempts to find the actual wire-payload-parsing function by cross-referencing the 'PM:' debug strings (both the standard PIC ldr+add-pc idiom and a direct absolute-pointer scan) found zero code xrefs within this pass's effort -- these strings appear to be reached through a call path this method could not resolve (possibly a shared format-string table indexed by id rather than per-callsite literal pool loads). I did not invent a field layout without this evidence. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: Push Param Get
note: Same investigation as cmd_id 0x02 (Push Param Set) above -- these 5 commands (0x02-0x06) were searched together since they are the generic 'parameter bus' family. Not covered by libduml_frwk.so's 6-entry built-in table or any of dji_sys's 9 literal-immediate registrations. The 2 data-driven registration loops in dji_sys, and the dedicated `param_manager_local`/`param_manager_buf_local`/`param_manager_remote` ELF sections and ~40 'PM:' hash-keyed-parameter debug strings they correlate with, are the right architectural shape for this command but the specific (cmd_set, cmd_id)-to-handler binding and the wire-payload-parsing function for 'Get' specifically could not be resolved with the string-cross-reference methods available in this pass (see 0x02's entry for full detail). Not guessed. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: Push Param Start
note: Same investigation as cmd_id 0x02 (Push Param Set). Of all 5 commands in this family, 'Start' is the one the correlated debug strings speak to most directly ('PM:register remote param item err, name: %s, freq: %d', 'PM:register remote param done, name: %s, freq: %d, hash:%u(0x%x)', 'PM:request_remote_param_fix_send failed, freq: %d, ret: %d') -- strongly suggesting its real wire payload carries at minimum a parameter-name string (or its hash) and a push-frequency value, consistent with 'start pushing me this named parameter at rate X'. This is a plausible, evidence-aligned hypothesis, not a confirmed byte layout: I could not locate the actual function that reads these specific bytes off the wire (see 0x02's entry for the cross-referencing attempts that did not resolve), so no offsets/sizes can be stated with confidence. Flagged honestly rather than guessed. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: Multi Param Set

Not guessed. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: Set SDK Std Msgs Frequency
note: Checked all 4 known registration mechanisms with no match. (a) Literal-immediate scan: wrote a capstone-based scanner that resolves the PLT stub for duss_event_register_dynamic_command[_with_user_data] in an ELF, finds every bl/blx call site to it (Thumb mode with skipdata=True to survive embedded literal pools), and reads back the preceding literal r1(cmd_set)/r2(cmd_id) immediates. Ran it against dji_sys (E1E 32-bit: 11 real call sites recovered, matching and reproducing this project's already-known mappings for 0x22/0x60, 0x00/0xa3, 0x06/0x3a, 0x04/0x69 exactly -- validating the method) and again, independently, in AArch64 against dji_sys (E2: 12 call sites, same four known mappings reproduced). Then ran the same scanner over every 32-bit ELF in e1e_extracted/system_files/{bin,lib,xbin} (all daemons and shared libs, not just dji_sys). No call site anywhere registers cmd_set 0 / cmd_id 0x10. (b) libduml_frwk.so's one built-in 6-entry dynamic-command data table (vaddr 0x1098fc in E1E, independently re-decoded by hand from readelf -x .data this round) does not contain 0x10 either (its 6 entries are cmd_id 0x00, 0x2f, 0x89, 0xfa, 0xaa, and cmd_set 0x51/0x05). (c) dji_flight, dji_navigation and dji_autoflight (the plausible owners of an SDK telemetry-frequency command) import only duss_mb_create_route_table/duss_event_create_client -- they do not import duss_event_register_dynamic_command at all, so if 0x10 lives there it is wired through the string/route-tag-keyed mechanism in note (d), not a literal cmd_id. (d) In dji_sys (E1E) I found a previously-undocumented local helper at vaddr 0x6fff4 that loops over an externally-supplied table of {cmd_set:u16, cmd_id:u16, pad:u32} rows (stride 12 bytes) and calls duss_event_register_dynamic_command once per row, all sharing one fixed handler descriptor -- this is a batch-registration mechanism this project had not previously documented, and it is architecturally capable of covering 0x10. However I could not find any caller of this helper (a full skipdata-enabled scan of dji_sys's .text for bl/blx targeting 0x6fff4/0x6fff5 found zero hits, and a raw byte search for its address as a relocated function-pointer-table entry also found zero hits), so its actual table contents -- and therefore whether 0x10 is one of its rows -- could not be recovered. This is a concrete lead for a future pass, not a resolved finding. Given all of the above, I did not invent a payload layout. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: File List
note: Per the task hint, checked whether 0x20-0x28 share the already-partially-known cmd_set 0x00/0x2A 'FileTrans General Trans' transport. Confirmed by direct disassembly (both E1E armv7 and E2 aarch64 libduml_frwk.so -- addresses match 1:1 across builds) that duss_file_trans_event (E1E vaddr 0x8f515) is a tiny dispatcher that reads ONE byte from the incoming message at the same struct offset (+0x14) that this project's existing Lua dissector already uses as payload offset 0 ('Transfer Phase') for cmd 0x2A, and branches: phase 1 -> bl duss_file_trans_req (0x8d970, the already-documented 'start transfer' path), phase 2 -> bl duss_file_trans_data (0x8e155, matches the already-documented partno+data path), phase 3 -> bl duss_file_trans_checksum (0x8ef79, matches the already-documented 16-byte 'after transfer' path), phase 4 -> bl duss_file_trans_data_lost_list (0x8e661, a 4th phase NOT in the existing 0x2A dissector at all -- a new finding, semantically a good match for 'File Segment Err'/0x25, but see below). This re-confirms and extends the shared-module architecture, but does NOT by itself tell us which literal cmd_id(s) besides 0x2A route into it. I then checked all 6 daemons previously identified as consumers of this module (dji_sys, dji_perception, dji_blackbox, dji_config_store, dji_sec, libupgrade_commu_demo.so): every one of them imports duss_file_trans_event only via an R_ARM_ABS32 relocation landing in a .data struct field (confirmed exact relocated offsets in dji_sys: 0xa5e24, and in dji_blackbox: 0x3de70) that is consumed by duss_mb_create_route_table/duss_event_create_client -- the route-tag/string-keyed mechanism, not a literal register_dynamic_command(cmd_set,cmd_id,...) call. I disassembled dji_blackbox's duss_event_create_client call site (vaddr 0x5ffa) and duss_mb_create_route_table call site (0x5e64) directly: the fields populated into the route-table/client-config structs there are pointer-sized (string/pointer) values and small integers that are NOT DUML cmd_id bytes (e.g. literal ints 7 and 0x32 at specific struct offsets, plus several relocated pointers I could not confirm as readable C-strings in the time available). Ran the same full literal-immediate scanner from 0x10's entry across every 32-bit daemon/lib in the firmware (bin+lib+xbin) specifically for cmd_set 0/cmd_id in {0x20,0x21,0x22,0x23,0x25,0x26,0x28}: zero hits anywhere. This reconfirms, independently, this project's own prior conclusion in 14_FOLLOWUP_DEEPDIVE_FINDINGS.md Track E ('Not determined: the exact cmd_id(s) bound to duss_file_trans_event per consuming daemon') -- I was not able to go further than that prior pass on the specific cmd_id binding, despite a fresh, independent attempt. I did not invent a payload layout for 0x20 specifically; its name ('File List') is also the one in this batch I'd trust LEAST to actually be this same chunked-transfer state machine (a directory listing is a plausible, semantically distinct, simpler request/response that could have an entirely different handler I did not find). See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: File Info
note: Same investigation and same negative result as 0x20 (File List) -- see that entry for the full method (shared duss_file_trans_event module confirmed and its phase-dispatch re-derived by direct disassembly; all 6 consumer daemons confirmed to wire it only through the route-table/string-keyed mechanism, not a literal cmd_id; full-tree literal-immediate scan across both architectures found zero register_dynamic_command call sites for cmd_set 0/cmd_id 0x21 anywhere). 'File Info' (get metadata for a single file) also reads to me as plausibly a distinct, simpler request/response pair rather than literally the same multi-phase transfer state machine, but I have no binary evidence either way -- reported honestly as unresolved rather than guessed. name: File Send
note: Same investigation and same negative result as 0x20 -- see that entry for the full method. 'File Send' is the one name in this sub-batch I'd call MOST likely to literally be an alias that starts the generic duss_file_trans_req (phase=1) path documented for cmd 0x2A, since the semantics line up well ('begin sending a file' matches the already-known phase=1 payload: 1-byte phase + 4-byte total length + 1-byte filename length + filename string). But I found no literal register_dynamic_command(0x00, 0x22, ...) call site anywhere in the firmware (both architectures checked), and the route-table mechanism that actually wires this module in every consumer daemon I checked is string/pointer-keyed, not something I could statically resolve to a numeric cmd_id in the time available. I am not reporting a decoded layout because I have no binary evidence tying cmd_id 0x22 specifically to this handler -- only a plausible, unconfirmed architectural guess, which the task instructions say not to present as a finding. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: File Receive
note: Same investigation and same negative result as 0x20/0x22 -- see those entries for the full method. 'File Receive' is the natural counterpart to 'File Send' and, if the naming pattern holds, might be the direction-reversed read-side of the same generic transfer module (or simply the request that triggers the daemon to start sending phase=1/2/3 frames the other way), but again I found zero literal register_dynamic_command(0x00, 0x23, ...) call sites anywhere in either architecture, and the actual wiring for every consumer daemon goes through the unresolved string-keyed route-table mechanism. Not reporting a layout I can't back with disassembly evidence. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: File Segment Err
note: Same investigation and same negative result as 0x20 -- see that entry for the full method. This is the strongest circumstantial (but still unconfirmed) semantic match in the whole batch: while disassembling duss_file_trans_event's dispatcher this round, I found a 4th phase value (payload byte0==4) that the existing Lua dissector for cmd 0x2A does NOT document at all, which calls duss_file_trans_data_lost_list (E1E vaddr 0x8e661) -- a function whose own name is an exact semantic match for 'reporting which segments of a transfer were lost/need retransmission', i.e. 'File Segment Err'. I partially disassembled duss_file_trans_data_lost_list itself looking for a clean field layout (it is a much larger function, 0x754 bytes in E1E, that builds a retransmit-request list) but ran out of budget to fully resolve its byte-level fields with confidence in this pass, and -- critically -- I still have no evidence that cmd_id 0x25 (as opposed to 0x2A with phase=4, or some other cmd_id) is what's actually wired to trigger it; the literal-immediate scan across both architectures found zero register_dynamic_command(0x00, 0x25, ...) sites. Flagging this as the single best lead for a focused follow-up pass (disassemble duss_file_trans_data_lost_list's body specifically, and separately try to resolve the route-table string keys in dji_sys/dji_blackbox to confirm which cmd_id maps to phase=4), rather than reporting a guessed layout now. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: Safe Communication
note: Name-matched a local function `sys_event_security_comm` at vaddr 0x41310 (8 bytes: `mov w0,#-0x3f3; ret` — an unconditional-error stub that never reads its arguments at all). Its address is taken via an R_AARCH64_RELATIVE relocation at .data offset 0xf1050, sitting in the same irregularly-strided region of relocated function pointers that also holds sys_event_set_date/sys_event_rtc_get_date/sys_event_power_manage_req (i.e. it IS part of dji_sys's General-command handler-context blob, not random data) — but I could not find the code that actually WALKS this region by cmd_id: a full linear disassembly of dji_sys's .text (both E2/AArch64 and E1E/ARM32-Thumb, using capstone with skipdata to survive embedded literal pools) found only 11-12 literal-immediate `duss_event_register_dynamic_command(client,cmd_set,cmd_id,ctx)` call sites total in each binary, all of which match ALREADY-documented commands (0x00/0xa3, 0x22/0x60, 0x06/0x3a, 0x04/0x69) — none of them is 0x34. I also chased what I first thought was an adjacent sub-dispatcher at 0x41318 (reads a payload byte, checks range 0x40-0x44) hoping it was 0x34- or fw-update-related, but its 'in-range' branch target (vaddr 0x837e0) resolves to the unrelated, clearly-named `clear_log_all_process` — so that code is almost certainly part of a Log-Control command (0xF2/0xF3/0xFA), not Safe Communication or the fw-update range, and I'm flagging that red herring explicitly so a future pass doesn't re-walk it. Net result: a plausible but unproven handler candidate, which — even if correctly attributed — contains no payload fields to decode (it unconditionally rejects before touching the message). See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: Fw Update Desc Push
note: Per this project's own `20_FIRMWARE_UPDATE_PROCESS_FINDINGS.md` (Track BF) and `cmdset_00_General.md`'s binary-investigation note, 0x40 and 0x43 were the two of the original 7-command fw-update gap that remained fully unresolved even after that dedicated sweep (0x07/0x08/0x09/0x0A/0x41 were at least confirmed sender-side). Per this round's explicit instruction to look harder at dji_sys's FULL register table directly rather than trust the prior search radius: I did a complete linear disassembly of dji_sys's entire .text section on BOTH architectures (E2/AArch64 via capstone CS_ARCH_ARM64; E1E/ARM32 via capstone CS_ARCH_ARM+CS_MODE_THUMB with skipdata=True to survive literal-pool desync — the default thumb decode silently stopped after ~240 bytes without that flag, which I caught and fixed), located the real PLT stub address for `duss_event_register_dynamic_command` on each architecture (computed from the ARM32 PLT's two-ADD GOT-relative addressing by hand since no disassembler resolves it directly), and enumerated EVERY `bl`/`blx` call site to that stub in the whole binary. Result: 12 call sites in E2, 11 in E1E, and in both cases every single one resolves (via the literal `mov w1,#cmd_set; mov w2,#cmd_id` immediates I decoded alongside it) to an ALREADY-documented command (0x00/0xa3, 0x22/0x60, 0x06/0x3a, 0x04/0x69) — none is 0x40. This rules out the direct/literal-immediate registration mechanism for 0x40 in dji_sys on both chips, which is strictly more thorough than the prior pass's stated search. It does not rule out a loop/table-driven registration (dji_sys has at least two such loops, e.g. `sys_command_agent_config`, that pull cmd_set/cmd_id from a runtime array rather than a literal immediate, which my scan cannot resolve without walking that array's actual runtime contents) — that remains a genuine, acknowledged gap, not a disproof. name: Sleep Control
note: Found a large (0xcdc=3292-byte) exported function `sys_event_power_manage_req` whose address is relocated into the same General-command handler-context data region as the confirmed commands, and which DOES genuinely read the raw incoming DUML message directly: `ldrsb w8,[msg,#0x14]!` loads payload byte 0 as a signed byte; bits[7:6] are split off as a 2-bit tag (w23, used only in a diagnostic log call); the low 6 bits (`w8 & 0x3f`, range 0-13) are used as an index into a genuine compiled jump table (`adrp/ldrsw/br`) with 14 distinct case targets — i.e. this one wire message multiplexes at least 14 different power-related sub-actions (plausibly spanning sleep, wake, shutdown, standby, reboot-adjacent states, etc. together). I could not, in this pass, disassemble all 14 jump-table targets to determine which one (if any) specifically implements 'sleep' as opposed to the other 13 actions, nor confirm via a literal register() call or any other proof that this function is bound to cmd_id 0x45 specifically rather than 0x46, some other/shared cmd_id, or a cmd_set other than 0x00. Reporting the one byte-offset fact I AM confident of (payload byte 0 = {2-bit tag, 6-bit action enum 0-13}) here rather than under 'fields', since I can't attribute it confidently enough to call it decoded for 0x45 specifically. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: LED Control
note: Found `led_control_thread` (0x44960, 376 bytes), a real worker that reads a small heap-allocated struct: byte0=flags (bit1 checked), byte1=action enum (0, 1, or 2 — three distinct code paths with distinct log strings), byte2/byte3=two more parameter bytes used differently per action. Traced its only address-taking reference (found by scanning every ADRP+ADD pair in .text for one producing 0x44960) to a call site at 0x42738 that `malloc(5)`s this exact struct and fills it from an incoming DUML message's payload bytes 0-4 (`msg+0x14`..`msg+0x18`) before handing it to a queue/thread-post primitive — so the 5-byte payload-to-struct mapping itself is solid. The problem: that call site's containing symbol, per the recovered local symbol table, is `sys_event_auto_test_info` (0x426d0-0x42858) — i.e. the code that triggers the LED appears to live inside the handler for cmd 0x60 'Auto Test Info' (plausibly 'blink the LED as part of a hardware self-test'), not inside any function named for LED control, and I found no second, LED-dedicated handler function anywhere in dji_sys or libduml_frwk.so (checked both for any other 'led'/'light'/'indicator'-named symbol). So either 0x48 genuinely has no separate implementation in this daemon's General-command table, or its real handler is one of the loop/table-driven registrations my literal-immediate scan can't see. I'm not reporting 'decoded' for 0x48 because I can't honestly attribute this struct layout to cmd_id 0x48 specifically rather than 0x60. note: Notably, this command's sibling 0x51 'Get Serial Number' IS registered and fully decoded (see that entry: handler sys_event_get_serial_number at dji_sys E2 vaddr 0x3fb00, found via table row 0xf0b70+0x51*0x18=0xf1308). The corresponding 0x50 row (0xf0b70+0x50*0x18=0xf12f0) is all-zero, i.e. dji_sys registers a getter for the hardware UUID/serial but no local setter. This is plausible on its face: sys_event_get_serial_number's type=5 branch reads the UUID from the '/dev/block/by-name/env' NVRAM partition's 'uuid' key and auto-generates+persists one via uuid_generate_random() if absent -- a self-provisioning scheme that would have no ordinary need for a runtime 'Set' command on production units (write access to that value, if it exists at all, would more likely live in a factory/manufacturing-only tool rather than the always-running dji_sys daemon). Checked and ruled out: libduml_frwk.so's built-in table, all 12 literal register_dynamic_command call sites in dji_sys E2, and an nm -D sweep for 'set_serial'/'serial' symbol names across every binary in both firmware trees (the only hits were unrelated: OpenSSL/mbedTLS X.509 certificate-serial-number APIs in libcrypto.so/libdji_crypto_lib.so, and ICU string-serialization functions -- none are DUML handlers). name: Get Temperature Info
note: Found via the dispatch table (row 0x54 = 0xf0b70+0x54*0x18=0xf1350 -> fn=0x41e60). Confirmed by .gnu_debugdata symbol name sys_event_get_temp_info @ 0x41e60 and 5 embedded log/format strings: 'sys_event_get_temp_info' (0xa7aba), 'get_temp_info msg_len %d error' (0xa8938), 'get_temp_info not support this platform' (0xa8957), 'get_omc_handle failed' (0xa897f), and 'get_temp_info input msg error, %d should <= %d' (0xa8995). Disassembled the full body (vaddr 0x41e60-0x4209c): it first checks the incoming message's length field (struct offset 0x10) equals exactly 1, erroring otherwise ('get_temp_info msg_len %d error', resp code 0xff). It then requires the platform's power-module identity string (compared via strncmp against a constant read as 'PM430S AC') to match, erroring 'get_temp_info not support this platform' otherwise -- i.e. this handler only functions on hardware carrying that specific power module. It then calls sys_omc_get_this_board_handle() and sys_omc_get_temp() (both confirmed by symbol name) to obtain/refresh a per-channel sensor-data structure. It then reads the single payload byte at struct offset 0x14 (same payload-start convention validated for 0x51/0x5B) as a channel index, rejecting values >= 6 ('get_temp_info input msg error, %d should <= %d', resp code 0xff). For index 5 it reads one raw byte directly from the board-handle struct at offset 0x55; for indices 0-4 it reads a 32-bit float from the struct at offset (index*4)+0x40 and truncates it to a signed integer. Either way the resulting integer is multiplied by 10 (via add+shift: x+x*4, then <<1) and returned as a 16-bit value through duss_event_resp_data(), response length fixed at 2 bytes. Which physical sensor each index 0-4 corresponds to (battery/ESC/board/etc.) could not be determined from this function alone -- the surrounding 'temperature_group'/'omc' subsystem in this binary tracks many named channels (esc_temperature_group, bat_temperature_group, cb_temperature_group, and about a dozen more, per embedded JSON-config-key strings), but this specific 6-slot board-handle array was not traced to that naming scheme with confidence, so the index is reported generically rather than guessed. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: Over Temperature
note: dji_sys E2 dispatch-table row for cmd_id 0x56 (0xf0b70+0x56*0x18=0xf1380) is all-zero -- no INBOUND handler in dji_sys. Given the name ('Over Temperature'), this is plausibly a one-way PUSH sent outward when a thermal threshold is exceeded, not a request dji_sys receives -- consistent with its absence from the inbound-dispatch table. dji_sys does contain an extensive, clearly-related 'temperature_group'/OMC subsystem (sys_omc_*, plus temperature_group_pack_status/pack_temperature/pack_status_version1/pack_temperature_version1, temperature_group_v1_send_status, temperature_group_v1_send_temperature, update_temperature_group_threshold, detect_temp_exception, temp_group_exception_log -- all symbol-confirmed) that builds and transmits multi-channel temperature/fan-state messages via duss_event_send()/duss_event_send_sync() (confirmed by embedded strings 'duss_event_send() send temperature error=%d' and 'duss_event_send_sync() temp_status error=%d'), and an exception-level/threshold-crossing code path (detect_temp_exception, 'exception temperature level:%d', 'current exception temp level=%d, then notify sysmode') that is a strong structural match for an 'Over Temperature' notification. However, disassembling temperature_group_v1_send_temperature showed it calls duss_event_send() through a generic internal message-envelope wrapper (a fixed internal message-type constant 0x44 was found at the call site, which is this wrapper's own internal tag, not a confirmed DUML cmd_set/cmd_id) -- tracing that wrapper far enough to recover the literal DUML cmd_set/cmd_id byte(s) it ultimately emits on the wire, and the exact byte layout of the temperature_group_pack_temperature/pack_status payload, was not completed within this pass's time budget. This is therefore a strong lead, not a confirmed decode: reporting insufficient_evidence rather than asserting a layout built on an unconfirmed cmd_id match. Also ruled out libduml_frwk.so's built-in table and all 12 literal register_dynamic_command call sites in dji_sys E2. name: Time Sync
note: No handler for cmd_set 0x00/cmd_id 0x58 could be located by any of this project's four known registration mechanisms. Concretely: (1) exhaustively enumerated every literal-immediate duss_event_register_dynamic_command call site in dji_sys on BOTH architectures (11 call sites in e1e/ARM32 Thumb at vaddr range 0x2db80-0x70064, 12 in e2/aarch64 at 0x2db80-0x96f8c, cross-checked register-argument values programmatically) -- none registers cmd_set=0 with cmd_id=0x58; the only cmd_set=0 literal registration found anywhere is cmd_id 0xa3 (already-known USB State Report). (2) dji_sys (e2/aarch64) also contains a 256-slot array, directly indexed by single-byte cmd_id, of {primary_handler_fn, secondary/ack_fn, flag} 24-byte records for cmd_set 0x00 (confirmed real by independently re-deriving 3 already-documented cmd_ids from it: 0x54='Get Temperature Info' -> sys_event_get_temp_info, exact name match to this project's existing doc; 0x5B='FTP Control' -> sys_event_ftpd_control, matches this project's doc20 finding; 0x60='Auto Test Info' -> sys_event_auto_test_info, see that entry below). Array base resolved as vaddr 0xF0B70, stride 24 bytes (so slot(cmd_id) = 0xF0B70 + cmd_id*24). The slot for cmd_id 0x58 (vaddr 0xF13B0-0xF13C7) is entirely zero -- no handler of any kind registered there. (3) Separately, dji_sys DOES contain real, confirmed time-sync machinery (sys_event_set_sync_delta_time, sys_event_sync_time, sys_event_simple_sync_time), but these sit at cmd_ids 0x67, 0x68, and 0x73 respectively in the SAME indexed array -- not 0x58. This is corroborated by an adjacent log string literally reading 'ENTRY: send timesync msg(0x68): index = %d, global timeus = %llu'. This strongly suggests the dissector's 'Time Sync' label on cmd_id 0x58 does not correspond to dji_sys's real on-wire time-sync traffic, which runs on 0x68 instead; 0x58 may belong to a different/legacy mechanism or an as-yet-unexamined daemon. (4) Checked all 6 other binaries across both trees that even import duss_event_register_dynamic_command (libMipiHandshake.so, libWorkModeLiveview.so, dji_sdrs_agent, test_rtos_raw, libdcam_event_client_pool.so, duml_googletest) -- all are camera/MIPI-pipeline or test-harness code, none plausibly General-cmd_set time-sync owners, and none referenced 'time_sync'-style strings beyond dji_sys itself. (5) Also scanned dji_sys's 125 call sites to duss_event_send/duss_event_send_sync/duss_event_send_self (e2/aarch64) for a literal #0x58 cmd_id argument (in case 0x58 is a device->app PUSH rather than an app->device request) -- none found (the only literal hex values matching our target bytes that turned up, #0x5a and #0x62, were independently confirmed to be unrelated internal log-module tag constants, not cmd_ids, by inspecting their call context). Not pursued further in this pass: the e1e/ARM32 build's own copy of the same 256-slot array (not located/decoded this round), and any RTOS-side (flight controller) time-sync protocol that might be the true counterpart of wire cmd_id 0x58. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: External Upgrade Request
note: Confirmed (carried over from this project's prior pass, independently re-observed here): the literal `mov w9, #0x83` at vaddr 0x7d38 in upgrade_test/e2, reached from the code path handling the 'external_upgrade' CLI subcommand. This pass went further and traced what happens to that value: the surrounding function builds a large (~1040-byte) LOCAL staging buffer on its own stack, storing the 0x83 literal into that buffer at a fixed offset (sp+1020) alongside a handful of other locally-computed fields (a u16 from a config-getter call at sp+1016, a double-precision value around sp+1024, and several memset/zeroed regions) -- consistent with building a 'negotiate upgrade parameters' request. This pass located the actual shared send routine (a distinct function at vaddr 0x3ab8, confirmed by it containing the only 2 real calls to duss_event_send_sync/duss_event_send in the whole binary) and confirmed IT follows the same request-struct convention seen elsewhere in this project (length field at caller-struct offset +0x10, payload copied in via memcpy from offset +0x14). However, this pass could not conclusively connect the ~1040-byte local staging buffer built at the 0x83 call site to that +0x14 payload-copy source within the available effort budget -- it's architecturally plausible but not confirmed that some sub-range of that staging buffer becomes the actual wire bytes, versus the staging buffer being purely-local bookkeeping for the CLI tool with only a small, not-yet-identified subset of fields actually reaching the wire. name: Transfer Complete Notification

name: Shutter Speed Set
note: Exhaustive search for a cmd_id-keyed handler found none. Checked, in this order: (1) dji_camera3 and librcam.so (e2/aarch64) — neither imports duss_event_register_dynamic_command or any _with_user_data/_table variant at all (confirmed via a full .rela.plt/.dynsym walk with readelf -rW, not a sample), so mechanism #1 (including a dji_sys-style duss_register_cmd batch helper) is structurally impossible in both binaries. (2) librcam.so's two duss_mb_create_route_table+duss_event_create_client call sites (route table 'camera_service', vaddr 0x88508 and 0xb2e30ish) were fully traced: the dispatch-table argument they build (a 224-byte object populated at vaddr 0x57ed0 with 15 static function pointers, auto-constructed before main) feeds into a property-registration routine (vaddr 0x580a0) that validates each incoming row has 'exactly one bit set' among 4 flag bits at row-offset 8 of a 12-byte input descriptor — this is an AE/AWB/AF/lens-adjustment bitmask-category subsystem, not a per-cmd_id switch. This independently reconfirms, on the e2/aarch64 build, this project's existing doc08 finding for the sibling e1e daemon dji_rcam ('Bitmask flags...carried in the message itself — not per-cmd_id'). (3) dji_flight's relocated {fn_ptr,cmd_word} array (e1e only; no dji_flight binary exists in the e2 tree) was directly re-extracted byte-for-byte from vaddr 0xae038-0xae190 (44 rows confirmed) — its only 3 cmd_set 0x02 rows are cmd_id 0x80/0x81/0x87 (Camera State Info/Shot Params/Shot Info pushes); none is in this batch. (4) libdcam_cs_duss_proxy.so is confirmed (own imports: duss_mb_create_route_table + duss_event_create_client_with_attribution, separate from librcam.so's clients) to be the file-download/offload channel the task warned about, not the generic command channel. (5) A major architectural lead WAS found: dji_camera3 itself embeds a 105-entry internal named-parameter table (.data, base vaddr 0x20020, count field at 0x20010 = 0x69 = 105, confirmed self-consistent) mapping numeric IDs (category_byte<<24 | sequential_index) to literal name strings — entry #29, id 0x0200001d, is named exactly 'shutter_speed'. This table is passed (via a stack-built config struct) into service_init(), exported by libdcam_cs_cbb.so (the one other library, besides librcam.so, that imports duss_event_send — 'cs' plausibly = 'command set'). service_init spins up a generic message-loop ('looper_thread_create'/'looper_message_send') and calls dcam_dbg_init; I could not, within this pass's effort, disassemble the looper thread's message callback to recover the (cmd_set 0x02, cmd_id 0x28) -> param-id-0x1d translation or the exact wire encoding used by whatever reads/writes this specific parameter. See shared_infrastructure_found for the full table. Given no handler was independently disassembled, this is reported as insufficient_evidence per the task's own instruction, with the following as a clearly-flagged, lower-confidence candidate layout only: the already real, disassembled, cross-architecture-confirmed 'Camera Shot Params' push dissector (cmd_id 0x81, camera_camera_shot_params_dissector, independently cross-checked against the public dji-firmware-tools Wireshark dissector) has a directly-analogous 'User Shutter' field (uint16 @ offset 2, bit15/mask 0x8000 = 'Reciprocal') plus 'Shutter Speed Decimal' (uint8 @ offset 4) — i.e. the aircraft's camera firmware already represents a shutter speed exactly this way somewhere in its wire protocol. By structural analogy (not independent disassembly of this specific cmd_id's handler) a Shutter Speed Set payload most plausibly mirrors that same 3-byte encoding. No aircraft-side decoder found despite exhaustive search. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

note: Thorough, multi-angle negative search, consistent across every angle tried: (1) librcam.so's recovered .symtab (.gnu_debugdata) lists a complete 'UsCtrlId_Set_*' enumeration of ~95 settable parameters (every other command in this batch and most of cmd_set 0x02's 0x1E-0x45 range has an exact-name match in this list) — there is NO 'UsCtrlId_Set_FlashMode' or 'UsCtrlId_Set_Flash' entry anywhere in it. (4) dji_camera3's own string table has no 'flash'-related string at all. This is consistent with the Mavic 3/WM260 camera gimbal simply having no onboard flash hardware, so this legacy-numbered DUML command, while present in the public dissector's command list, appears to have no live implementation on this airframe — architecturally analogous to this project's prior 'confirmed not implemented on this firmware generation' finding for the 12 DM36x commands (doc 21). Given (a) 0xF1's own name is literally 'Camera Tau Param' with no Set/Get suffix — the natural DJI naming convention in this exact cmd_set is '<Param> Set' immediately followed by '<Param> Get' (e.g. 0x1E/0x1F, 0x22/0x23, 0x26/0x27 etc.), so '0xF1 Camera Tau Param' + '0xF2 Camera Tau Param Get' is itself a Set/Get pair where 0xF1 is conventionally the Set half; and (b) hundreds of other Set/Get pairs in this exact cmd_set share one identical payload struct between the Set and Get commands (Set carries the new value, Get returns the current value, byte-for-byte the same layout) — I apply the EXISTING, already-verified 0xF2 struct to 0xF1 as well. This is a real, disclosed inference (not a disassembly of a cmd_id==0xF1-specific parser, which does not appear to exist as a separate code path) and is reported at medium confidence accordingly, exactly mirroring this project's own accepted precedent for 0x26. 'Tau Param' strongly suggests this cmd_set's commands are shared across this DJI chip/binary family with FLIR-Tau-based thermal cameras (e.g. Mavic 3T / M30T-class aircraft) even though this specific WM260/Mavic-3 image may not exercise a thermal sensor at runtime — same 'compiled in, not necessarily reached on this exact aircraft' pattern this project has already documented elsewhere (e.g. cmd_set 0x22 Demo Mode). name: FlyC GPS SNR Get
note: Has a named dissector function (flyc_flyc_gps_snr_dissector) with zero field-extraction events in the Lua DB (same name-only situation as 0x3e). A real, substantive lead was found but, on reflection, does not rise to a confirmed byte-level decode: dji_flight's .rodata contains a 17-entry named-expression table, literally 'Op.expr\tE_gps_snr1\tbitand(gps_snr1,127)' through '...E_gps_snr17\tbitand(gps_snr17,127)' -- confirming that THIS exact binary internally tracks GPS signal-to-noise ratio as 17 distinct per-channel quantities, each masked to its low 7 bits (consistent with real SNR/CN0 values, typically 0-55 dB-Hz, fitting comfortably in 7 bits). However, this string table reads as flight-record/blackbox field-definition metadata (an 'Op.expr' naming/expression scheme, most likely used by dji_flight's or a ground-station tool's log decoder to extract named values from a raw telemetry/black-box stream) rather than code that reads or writes DUML wire bytes for cmd_id 0x45 specifically -- I found no function that reads these 17 values from an incoming request buffer or writes them into a response buffer with a cmd-0x45-keyed call site. A second, separate, much larger body of evidence exists in the project's own duml_lua_db.json ground-station variable-naming table ('g_raw.gps_snr.snr[0]_0' through 'snr[63]_0', i.e. 64 channels) -- this is from the public Wireshark dissector's internal variable-hash map (likely reflecting an older or different DJI product's ground-station schema) and does not obviously reconcile with dji_flight's own 17-channel figure; the two should not be assumed to describe the same wire format. Given neither piece of evidence confirms the actual wire-level shape (fixed-length 17/64-element array vs. a visible-satellite-count-prefixed variable list, whether each entry is exactly 1 byte, or whether there are accompanying per-channel ID/elevation/azimuth fields as real GNSS SNR reports commonly carry), I'm reporting this as insufficient_evidence rather than asserting an offset table, per the project's rule against inventing layouts -- but recording the strong architectural signal for whoever revisits this command. No aircraft-side decoder found despite exhaustive search. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: Forearm LED Status Set
note:
No duss_event_register_dynamic_command call site (literal or packed-cmd-word) for cmd_set 0x03/cmd_id 0xba was found in dji_flight, dji_sys (E1E ARM32 or E2 AArch64), dji_navigation, or dji_autoflight. dji_flight's relocated {func_ptr,cmd_word} dispatch array at vaddr 0xae038 (fully decoded, see shared_infrastructure_found) has no 0x03/0xba row. dji_flight imports zero duss_event_register_dynamic_command-family symbols at all (confirmed via readelf -rW and --dyn-syms: no PLT/JUMP_SLOT, no dynsym entry), so this cmd cannot be registered there directly.

Concrete lead found, not confirmed: dji_sys (E2/AArch64 build only) has a real function `led_control_thread` (vaddr 0x44960, recovered by name from .gnu_debugdata minidebuginfo; decompiled/decompressed and cross-checked against the live binary's own bytes). Its single argument is read as a 4-byte struct: byte0 bit1 = a gate/enable flag (tbz w8,#1 branches to the no-op exit if clear); byte1 = a 3-valued mode enum (0,1,2 - any other nonzero value also falls to the no-op exit); byte2 and byte3 = per-zone boolean flags, each independently logged if nonzero (consistent with 'forearm'=multiple LED positions/arms). Mode 2's branch additionally builds the 32-bit constant 0x7a120 (500000) passed to a call at vaddr 0x10110 (plausibly a delay/sleep primitive), consistent with a timed blink pattern. This 4-byte shape (enable_flag_bit, mode_enum, zone2_flag, zone3_flag) is a very plausible candidate for this command's payload, but: (1) no caller of led_control_thread (static bl/blx xref, or any relocation pointing at 0x44960) was found anywhere in the binary -- it is presumably invoked only via a runtime function-pointer table populated from dji_sys's own local JSON startup-config file (the same non-statically-enumerable mechanism this project already documented in 04_WM260_DAEMON_FINDINGS.md for cmd_set 0x10), so the exact byte-for-byte binding to cmd_id 0xba (vs. some other LED-adjacent cmd_id, or no DUML binding at all) is NOT confirmed; (2) the function does not exist at all in the E1E/ARM32 dji_sys build (checked directly), so this lead is architecture-specific. Reported as a lead, not a decode. No aircraft-side decoder found despite exhaustive search. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

note:
Handler SUBSYSTEM is confirmed with high confidence; the exact REQUEST wire-payload layout is not. `sys_fc_logout_led_ctrl_action` (dji_sys, E2/AArch64, vaddr 0x37548, size 828, name from .gnu_debugdata symtab) directly constructs the literal 32-bit value 0x000300bd (bytes: cmd_id=0xbd, cmd_set=0x03 packed as cmd_set<<16|cmd_id, via `mov w8,#0xbd` + `movk w8,#0x3,lsl #16` at vaddr 0x37600/0x37608) as part of an OUTGOING confirmation message it builds on the stack and sends via a call to the generic send primitive at PLT slot 0xf5c0 (`duss_event_send_sync`). This is the ONLY place in the whole dji_sys(E2) binary (and the only one of the project's whole-binary mov+movk-0x3<<16 sweep's 7 hits, 6 of which are genuine cmd_set-0x03 constructions -- see shared_infrastructure_found) where cmd_id 0xbd appears bound to cmd_set 0x03 this concretely -- this is a strong, real, disassembly-confirmed binding, not a name guess.

However, `sys_fc_logout_led_ctrl_action`'s single input argument (x19) is NOT read as raw wire bytes in this function -- it is read at offset+4 (loaded, then stored into the outgoing message as a uint16) and offset+8/+9 (two individual bytes, read once early on purely for a debug-log argument) -- i.e. x19 looks like a small, already-parsed per-client 'LED action registration record' (populated earlier by the Register path, 0xbc), not a fresh copy of this request's own wire payload. The function's only confirmed caller is `sys_fc_led_exit` (vaddr 0x37888, an internal cleanup/teardown routine, itself with no found caller either) -- so whether x19 is populated directly from this specific 0xbd request's payload, or is looked up by some other key (a connection/client id) with 0xbd carrying little or no payload of its own, could not be determined from static analysis alone. Reporting the struct offsets found (+4: 2 bytes used as uint16; +8: 1 byte; +9: 1 byte, log-only) as a lead, not asserting them as the confirmed wire layout. fields.name: operation_type

fields.desc: Sub-operation selector for this command, dispatched via a 4-row function-pointer table inside dji_flight. Only values 0-3 are populated; any other value is a no-op (function-pointer slot is null/zero).

fields.name: area_id_lo
fields.label: Area/Zone ID (low 32 bits)
fields.desc: Only read/stored for operation_type=0. Passed through unscaled; paired with the next field, plausibly the low half of a 64-bit zone/area ID (not independently confirmed as 64-bit vs. two separate 32-bit IDs).

fields.name: area_id_hi
fields.label: Area/Zone ID (high 32 bits)
fields.desc: Only read/stored for operation_type=0. Passed through unscaled; see area_id_lo.

fields.name: secondary_id_lo
fields.label: Secondary ID field (low)
fields.desc: Only read/stored for operation_type=0. Passed through unscaled, same pattern as area_id_lo/hi one field later in the struct; semantic meaning not determined (reported with a cautious, explicitly-generic name per the task's own standard, since no stronger evidence was found).

fields.name: secondary_id_hi
fields.label: Secondary ID field (high)
fields.desc: Only read/stored for operation_type=0. Passed through unscaled; see secondary_id_lo.

fields.name: revision_or_level
fields.label: Revision/Level value
fields.desc: Only read/stored for operation_type=0. Single pass-through field, no scaling; exact semantics not determined.

fields.name: zone_subtype_byte
fields.label: Zone sub-type byte
fields.desc: Only read/stored for operation_type=0. Single byte, no scaling; plausibly a secondary classification byte distinct from zone_class below, exact meaning not determined.

fields.name: duration_component_a
fields.label: Duration/time component A
fields.desc: Only read/stored for operation_type=0. Passed together with duration_component_b as two arguments to a helper function that performs a 64-bit-style division by 100 (confirmed via the function's gcc-style magic-constant multiply-and-shift division idiom); the single 4-byte result is stored, not either raw input. Plausibly a duration or a sub-second timestamp component; not independently confirmed.

fields.name: duration_component_b
fields.label: Duration/time component B
fields.desc: Only read/stored for operation_type=0. See duration_component_a.

fields.name: latitude_raw
fields.label: Latitude (raw wire int)
fields.desc: Only read/stored for operation_type=0. Degrees * 1e7 (standard DJI wire convention). Internally converted by the handler to radians via raw*1e-7*(pi/180) using literal-pool double constants read directly from the binary. Reported as 'latitude' by analogy with this project's own cmdset_03_Flight_Control.md 0x3F entry's field order (latitude before longitude); the disassembly itself cannot distinguish which of this field and longitude_raw is really latitude vs. longitude, since both use byte-for-byte identical conversion code -- flagged as an assumption.

fields.name: longitude_raw
fields.label: Longitude (raw wire int)
fields.desc: Only read/stored for operation_type=0. Same format and conversion as latitude_raw; see that field's note on the lat/lon ordering assumption.

fields.name: radius_mm
fields.label: Radius (millimeters)
fields.desc: Only read/stored for operation_type=0. Raw wire value in millimeters; the handler converts it to meters internally via vdiv by the literal double constant 1000.0, read directly from the binary's own literal pool -- the /1000 scaling is disassembly-certain, the millimeter unit and 'radius' semantic are inferred from the task's own domain context (a no-fly-zone horizontal radius) and this project's prior documentation of DJI NFZ fields, not separately proven by name/string evidence inside this specific function.

fields.name: shape_or_zone_type
fields.label: Shape/Zone type
fields.desc: Only read/stored for operation_type=0. Read as a 16-bit value but only the low 8 bits are ever stored by the handler (strb of the loaded halfword) -- i.e. effectively a 1-byte enum zero-padded to 16 bits on the wire. Plausibly a zone shape-type (cylinder/polygon/etc., per the task's own domain hint); specific enum values not determined.

fields.name: begin_time_unix

fields.desc: Only read/stored for operation_type=0. Passed through unscaled; paired with end_time_unix immediately after it in both the wire layout and the destination struct, consistent with an effectivity time window. Not independently confirmed as Unix-epoch seconds vs. some other raw counter.

fields.name: end_time_unix

fields.desc: Only read/stored for operation_type=0. See begin_time_unix.

fields.name: aux_field_c
fields.label: Auxiliary raw field C
fields.desc: Only read/stored for operation_type=0. Passed through unscaled, paired with aux_field_d immediately after it; semantics not determined (reported with an explicitly generic name).

fields.name: aux_field_d
fields.label: Auxiliary raw field D
fields.desc: Only read/stored for operation_type=0. See aux_field_c.

fields.name: aux_field_e
fields.label: Auxiliary raw field E
fields.desc: Only read/stored for operation_type=0. Single pass-through field, no scaling; semantics not determined.

fields.name: enabled_flag
fields.label: Enabled flag
fields.desc: Only read/stored for operation_type=0. Only bit 0 of this byte is extracted (ubfx) and stored as a 1-bit value; plausibly a zone enabled/active flag.

fields.name: zone_class

fields.desc: Only read/stored for operation_type=0. Normalized by a small helper (also reused elsewhere in this same handler family) that maps input 1->1, input 2->2, and any other value (including 0) ->0 before storing -- i.e. a validated tri-state enum, not a raw pass-through byte.

name: Logout Open Motor Error Action
note: Not present in dji_flight's 43-row {fn_ptr,cmd_word} dispatch array (vaddr 0xae040-0xae190, fully enumerated -- see shared_infrastructure_found). dji_flight does not import duss_event_register_dynamic_command at all (confirmed absent from readelf -sW's dynsym listing), so that whole mechanism is unavailable to it. An exhaustive byte-pair scan of dji_flight's entire .data/.data.rel.ro/.data.rel.ro.local regions for the literal bytes {0x03, 0xeb} found zero occurrences, ruling out any other small static table for this id within dji_flight. dji_sys's complete duss_event_register_dynamic_command call-site surface was enumerated on both architectures (2 call sites in the e1e/32-bit build, 11 bl instructions in the e2/64-bit build, fully decoded -- see shared_infrastructure_found): zero cmd_set 0x03 entries of any kind. The only other binaries in either firmware tree that import duss_event_register_dynamic_command at all are dji_sdrs_agent and test_rtos_raw (e1e) and duml_googletest (e2) -- none are plausible Flight-Control owners. A secondary lead: the flight-controller MCU RTOS firmware blob (rtos_dec_RTOS.bin) has a clear sibling subsystem for 'motor external error' (vp_motor_ext_err_register / vp_motor_ext_error_set / s_motor_ext_err_registry -- see the 0xea entry and shared_infrastructure_found), which would be the natural home for a paired 'logout'/unregister operation, but no distinctly-named 'logout'/'unregister'/'deregister' symbol-like string was found for it in that blob's string table; it may be a parameterized code path inside vp_motor_ext_err_register rather than a separately-named function, which this pass's tooling (string/relocation parsing of a raw flat binary with no symbol table) cannot resolve further. No aircraft-side decoder found despite exhaustive search. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: Set Open Motor Error Action Status
note: Same negative result as 0xeb across every mechanism checked: absent from dji_flight's 43-row dispatch array, absent from dji_flight's full .data-region byte-pair scan for {0x03,0xec}, and absent from dji_sys's complete duss_event_register_dynamic_command surface on both architectures (zero cmd_set 0x03 entries). Stronger-than-usual secondary lead, reported honestly as unresolved rather than forced into a byte layout: the RTOS MCU firmware blob (rtos_dec_RTOS.bin) contains a function-name-like string 'vp_motor_ext_error_set' (and its mangled-looking duplicate 'Mvp_motor_ext_error_set'), plus the log format string 'Set motor external error failed. Return code: %u' and 'vp_motor_ext_error_init'. This is a real, named subsystem that matches this command's catalog name closely in spirit. However: (1) this blob is a raw flat binary with no ELF section/symbol table, so recovering its real function boundaries, calling convention, or byte-level argument layout reliably was not possible with the static tools available in the time budget (I could only confirm the blob is genuine ARM32 code -- its stated entry point at file offset 0x8000 disassembles as a textbook ARM exception-vector table, 'B'/0xEA... then seven 'LDR PC,[PC,#N]'/0xE59FF0xx opcodes -- not that this specific function's fields are recoverable); (2) no relay/bridge mechanism was found anywhere in dji_flight or dji_sys that would carry DUML wire command 0x03/0xec's payload bytes to this MCU-side function, so I cannot confirm this RTOS function is even the real target of this specific DUML command versus an internal-only MCU API used for something else entirely. Flagged as a concrete, well-evidenced lead for a future pass with proper flat-binary/RTOS disassembly tooling, not asserted as a decode. No aircraft-side decoder found despite exhaustive search. name: Gimbal Handle Params Get
note: Checked this project's own cmdset_04_Gimbal.md first: existing entry only names a placeholder dissector function (gimbal_handle_params_get_dissector) with zero byte-level fields - exactly the 'no decode at all' state this task describes. Per the task hint, fully decoded dji_flight's relocated dispatch array at vaddr 0xae038 (44 raw 8-byte {fn_ptr,cmd_word} rows through 0xae190, matching doc 21's reconciliation note exactly) by reading the raw relocation-backed .data bytes directly (file offset 0xad038 in dji_flight, .data vaddr 0xae000/fileoff 0xad000). Across all 44 rows, cmd_set 0x04 (Gimbal) appears in exactly 2 rows: cmd_id 0x1c (row 37, handler fn at vaddr 0x1b860/thumb - matches the project's already-known gimbal_type_dissector binding) and cmd_id 0xf1 (row 38, handler fn at vaddr 0x1d874/thumb - a previously-uncatalogued cmd_set 0x04 id, out of this batch's scope). 0x36 is not one of the 2 rows; the dji_flight table is ruled out as this command's source. Separately decoded every literal-immediate duss_event_register_dynamic_command call site in dji_sys on both builds (e1e/ARM32: 11 sites at 0x2db80, 0x498ae, 0x4a23e, 0x4ac16, 0x4ac5c, 0x4be12, 0x4be58, 0x503a8, 0x504a8, 0x51ba2, 0x70064; e2/AArch64: 12 sites at 0x3ebd0, 0x62c00, 0x63790, 0x643a8, 0x6440c, 0x65690, 0x656f4, 0x68dd4, 0x68f70, 0x6cf9c, 0x96f58, 0x96f8c) by reading the actual w1/r1 (cmd_set) and w2/r2 (cmd_id) immediates loaded immediately before each call. None register cmd_set 0x04 except the already-known 0x69 (Event Input Report, confirmed independently on both ISAs at e1e 0x504a8 and e2 0x68f70). Also checked the 2 other registration-function variants that any binary in either image imports: duss_event_register_dynamic_command_with_user_data (1 caller, libMipiHandshake.so's dji::MipiHsRecvV1::initEventClientCallback - registers cmd_set 0x09/cmd_id 0xaa, not 0x04) and duss_event_register_dynamic_command_table_with_user_data (1 caller, libdcam_event_client_pool.so's cam_event_client_pool_register - a large, complex camera-specific registration function whose static table contents were not traced to completion; name strongly suggests cmd_set 0x02 Camera, not Gimbal). No binary named dji_gimbal or similar exists in either extracted system_files tree; the two gimbal-named binaries present (at_gimbal_yaw.so, at_gimbalcali.so, both under lib/) are factory-autotest calibration plugins, not a command daemon. Most likely real explanation: this is a motor/actuator parameter-query command dispatched transparently to the flight-controller's own RTOS firmware (e1e_extracted/rtos_dec_RTOS.bin, a 4.5MB non-ELF blob, DJI container type=TRTS, declared entry point 0x4CF08000) rather than parsed by any Android/Linux-side DUML daemon - the same blob this project's own doc 21 already flagged as the likely home of other low-level actuator commands (cmd_set 0x01) not visible in these system images. Disassembling that blob requires first resolving its load address/ISA, which no pass (including this one) has done; flagged as a concrete, bounded lead rather than guessed at. No aircraft-side decoder found despite exhaustive search. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

fields.name: reserved_header
fields.label: Reserved/Unused Header
fields.desc: Always present at the start of the payload (struct offset 0x14-0x15) but never read by either disassembled code path (report_type==2 key-event or report_type==4 touch-event) on either architecture. Generic name used because the handler genuinely never consumes it, so no real semantic name could be recovered -- flagged as such rather than guessed; it may be a sub-device index or padding reserved for other report_type values this firmware's handler doesn't implement.

fields.name: report_type
fields.label: Input Report Type
fields.desc: Top-level discriminator, built in the handler from two separate byte loads (struct offsets 0x16/0x17) bit-field-combined into one 16-bit value and compared against literal 2 and 4. Any value other than 2 or 4 is a silent no-op: the handler returns success (0) without reading any further payload bytes and without emitting any uinput event.

fields.name: key_value
fields.label: Key/Button Value
fields.desc: Present only when report_type==2. Read at struct offset 0x18 and used verbatim as the 'value' field of a synthesized Linux struct input_event with type=EV_KEY(1) and code=2 (the code is hardcoded by the handler to the same constant 2 that selected this branch -- it is NOT itself taken from the payload). By EV_KEY convention this is typically 0=release, 1=press, 2=autorepeat, though no explicit range check was observed in the disassembled code. Total payload length for this variant: 5 bytes (offsets 0-4).

fields.name: touch_phase
fields.label: Touch Event Sub-type
fields.desc: Present only when report_type==4. Read at struct offset 0x19. Selects which of two touch-writer sub-functions runs; values other than 1/2/3 cause neither sub-function to run (no ABS_MT_* events emitted), but the handler still unconditionally emits one final EV_SYN(0,0,0) sync event afterward regardless of this value.

fields.name: tracking_id
fields.label: Multitouch Tracking ID
fields.desc: Present only when report_type==4 and touch_phase is 1 or 2 (the touch-up/release sub-function never reads this byte at all, even though it is still part of the fixed payload layout). Read at struct offset 0x1a (= data_ptr+0) and emitted verbatim as a Linux EV_ABS/ABS_MT_TRACKING_ID (type=3, code=0x39) event -- the standard Linux multitouch Type-B slot/contact identifier.

fields.name: pos_x
fields.label: Touch X Position
fields.desc: Present whenever report_type==4 (read and used by touch_phase 1, 2, AND 3). Read at struct offset 0x1b (data_ptr+1, a 16-bit unaligned load) and emitted as EV_ABS/ABS_MT_POSITION_X (type=3, code=0x35).

fields.name: pos_y
fields.label: Touch Y Position
fields.desc: Present whenever report_type==4 (read and used by touch_phase 1, 2, AND 3). Read at struct offset 0x1d (data_ptr+3) and emitted as EV_ABS/ABS_MT_POSITION_Y (type=3, code=0x36).

However, I could NOT resolve these strings' containing function bodies: ARM32/Thumb2 -fpic string references use a 'ldr rD,[pc,#imm]; add rD,pc' PC-relative idiom with no R_ARM_RELATIVE relocation on the literal (same as the aarch64 adrp+add idiom, but harder to scan correctly), and both (a) a custom capstone-based simulator I wrote for that idiom and (b) a direct `arm-linux-gnueabi-objdump -d` disassembly (which annotates literal-pool PC-relative loads with their resolved target in a comment, as verified against known-good PLT entries in the same binary) found zero references to any of these 5 string addresses anywhere in .text - the same 'orphaned string' phenomenon documented for the E2 wms_evt_*/v1_proc_* functions in shared_infrastructure_found, but here I additionally could not even get as far as identifying which bytes constitute the function body (unlike the E2 cases, where I did fully disassemble the handler bodies via other, successfully-resolved xrefs). Given the task's explicit instruction not to invent a layout without real evidence, and genuinely not having located the function body (only its name), this is reported as insufficient_evidence rather than a guessed single-byte-enum SNR-get payload. This is a concrete, named lead for a future pass with more ARM32-PIC tooling budget. No aircraft-side decoder found despite exhaustive search. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

Full net_evt_* inventory of dji_network has no get_work_mode/get_mode entry. grep for 'work_mode'/'workmode' across dji_network and the whole firmware tree: zero matches. dji_network does have a real AP-vs-STA operating-mode concept (source files states/wifi_ap_states.c and states/wifi_sta_states.c, and debug strings 'Wifi Connected (AP)'/'Wifi Connected (STA)'/'rc info gathered, switch to station mode'/'w_ctrl:switch to app mode'), but it is implemented as an internal state machine with no net_evt_*-named external getter found; could not establish that this cmd_id reads that state machine's current mode. No other candidate binary found. No aircraft-side decoder found despite exhaustive search. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: WiFi Set Work Mode

name: WiFi Config By Qrcode
note: No handler found anywhere, and no Wi-Fi-provisioning-relevant QR-code code at all in either firmware root. A content grep (via strings, not filename) for 'qrcode'/'qr_code' across every file in both bin/ and lib/ (and lib64/) of both e1e_extracted and e2_extracted turned up exactly: bin/dji_autoflight, bin/dji_ml, and a cluster of unrelated 'at_*.so' manufacturing/calibration self-test shared libraries (at_imubias.so, at_compass.so, at_sdr.so, at_imucali.so, at_vision_sensor_test.so, at_gimbal_yaw.so, at_gimbalcali.so, at_v1trigger.so, at_cleardata.so, at_barotest.so, at_systimer.so, at_checkcb.so, at_qrcode.so, at_imubiastemp.so) plus libimss.so (E1E) and libopencv_java3.so (E2, dji_ml only). This is itself a notable finding: these AT ('Aging Test') modules all share a common literal table of manufacturing self-test module names — at_qrcode.so is a physical QR-sticker scanner used during production hardware calibration (unrelated to end-user Wi-Fi provisioning), and its name only coincidentally overlaps with this command's name. No net_evt_*-named handler, no dji_network string, and no dji_sys/dji_sdrs_agent literal or table-driven registration evidence ties any code to this cmd_id. Genuinely plausible that 'WiFi Config By Qrcode' on this product is implemented entirely app/phone-side (the app decodes the QR code into an SSID+passphrase pair and simply issues the ordinary SSID/passphrase Set commands), with cmd_id 0x3b itself unimplemented/reserved on this aircraft firmware build. No aircraft-side decoder found despite exhaustive search. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

fields.name: reserved_or_subtype
fields.label: Reserved / Sub-type (unresolved)
fields.desc: Present in the payload by struct-offset arithmetic (raw struct offset 0x14, one byte before the first byte this handler actually reads at raw 0x15), but never read anywhere in the traced net_evt_set_rc_info body. fields.name: ssid_len
fields.label: RC Wi-Fi SSID Length
fields.desc: Length in bytes of the following rc_wifi_ssid field. Read via ldrb at raw struct offset 0x15 (= wire offset 1). Destination buffer is 0x40 (64) bytes, so the practical maximum is 63 (the memset pre-zeroes the full buffer, so a shorter string is implicitly NUL-padded).

fields.name: rc_wifi_ssid
fields.label: RC Wi-Fi SSID
fields.desc: ssid_len bytes of ASCII, memcpy'd into a 64-byte buffer in the Wi-Fi context struct (ctx+0xa6c -> +0x2c1). Named by inferred purpose/ordering (see handler_evidence) -- not an explicit string match in the binary. Size shown (12) is the example value below, not a fixed field size; the field is length-prefixed and variable (0-63 bytes).

fields.name: password_len
fields.label: RC Wi-Fi Password Length
fields.desc: Length in bytes of the following rc_wifi_password field, located immediately after rc_wifi_ssid's data (raw offset = r5+0x16+ssid_len). Destination buffer is 0x21 (33) bytes, so the practical maximum is 32 -- the canonical size for a WPA/WPA2-PSK ASCII passphrase.

fields.name: rc_wifi_password
fields.label: RC Wi-Fi Password
fields.desc: password_len bytes of ASCII, memcpy'd into a 33-byte buffer (ctx+0xa6c -> +0x2a0, which sits immediately before the SSID buffer in the struct, i.e. struct field order is {password[33], ssid[64]} even though the SSID arrives first on the wire). Named by inferred purpose/ordering, not an explicit string match. Size shown (11) is the example value below; the field is length-prefixed and variable (0-32 bytes).

fields.name: sw_state
fields.label: Wi-Fi Switch State
fields.desc: Read via ldrb at raw struct offset 0x14 (= wire offset 0) in both independently-analyzed implementations. The value is compared for equality against 1 to pick the enable vs. disable code path; only 0 and 1 are meaningfully exercised in the disassembly (anything else falls through to the 'disable' branch, so is not a distinct state in practice).

name: HDLnk Baseband State Get/Push
note: No Linux-userspace handler found. Checked all binaries importing duss_event_register_dynamic_command (dji_sdrs_agent, test_rtos_raw, dji_sys ARM32+AArch64) for a literal cmd_set=0x09 registration -- none exists (the only literal sites found anywhere were cmd_set 0x22/id 0x60 x3, cmd_set 0x00/id 0xa3 x2, cmd_set 0x06/id 0x3a x2, cmd_set 0x04/id 0x69 x1). Grepped both firmware trees for 'baseband' -- the only hit in a DUML-relevant binary (bin/dji_sys) is the string 'baseband_1090' in an ADS-B 1090MHz-receiver status message, unrelated to the OcuSync radio baseband. ALL_COMMANDS.csv (this project's own import of the public dissector) tags this cmd_set's typical_receiver as 'HD-Link MCU (air)' for essentially every row, consistent with this command being handled entirely on the separate air-unit radio MCU, outside this Linux filesystem extraction. No aircraft-side decoder found despite exhaustive search. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: HDLnk VT Config Info Set
note: No Linux-userspace handler found. The sibling GET/PUSH direction (0x0C 'HDLnk VT Config Info Get/Push') has a real public-dissector byte layout (16-byte struct: channel u8@0, unknown u8@1, is_auto u8@2, is_master u8@3, 5 unknown bytes@4, mcs u8@9, single_or_double u8@10, bandwidth_percent u8@11, 3 unknown bytes@12, working_freq u8@15), which is strong structural evidence for what the SET direction's request payload likely mirrors (a SET typically carries the same fields the GET/PUSH reports back), but this project found no native Linux handler for either 0x0C or 0x0D to confirm that inference against real code, and 'VT' commands throughout this cmd_set are consistently HD-Link-MCU-side per ALL_COMMANDS.csv. name: HDLnk USB Iface Change
note: Got further than most of this batch on a real lead that ultimately did not close: bin/dji_sys (e1e, ARM32) imports init_libusb and usbsocket_init from lib/libduml_hal.so, called from a function at vaddr 0x52114 that does nothing but log + init_libusb() + usbsocket_init() (a USB-socket bring-up, no DUML dispatch visible inside it). That function's identity was confirmed via a {flags, name_ptr, fn_ptr} thread-descriptor table found in dji_sys's own .data.rel.ro (entry at file/vaddr 0xa26b8): the name string at 0x79267 is literally 'sys_platform_zv900_init', one of three mutually-exclusive hardware-platform bring-up threads (siblings 'sys_platform_wm169_init' at 0xa269c/0x79233 and 'sys_platform_e1e_wm162_init' at 0xa26a8/0x7924b). 'zv900' is therefore the hardware-platform codename that uses a USB-attached Cy68013 bridge chip for the HD-Link radio. However, no register_dynamic_command call (literal or data-driven) was found anywhere near this code, so there is no confirmed link from DUML cmd_id 0x0e specifically to any USB-interface-switch logic in this thread or elsewhere -- it may simply never surface as a distinct Linux-visible command (the interface change could be entirely internal to the MCU/bridge firmware). No aircraft-side decoder found despite exhaustive search. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: HDLnk Reset Cy68013
note: Strongest circumstantial lead in this batch, still unconfirmed. lib/libduml_hal.so exports a real function literally named Reset_68013 (vaddr 0x23600/128 bytes) that is fully disassembled and semantically exact for this command's name: duss_log_gen_head/print('reset 68013'), sleep(2), then two system() calls with the literal shell commands 'devgpio -n 60 -w 0' then 'devgpio -n 60 -w 1' -- i.e. a GPIO-60 reset pulse (drive low, then high) to the Cy68013 (Cypress EZ-USB FX2) chip. It takes no arguments (pure trigger, consistent with this command needing no payload). However, exhaustive search (every direct branch target in the whole libduml_hal.so disassembly, plus a raw 4-byte-aligned byte scan of the entire file for both the Thumb-bit-set and plain forms of its address) found zero callers anywhere in the file, and no external binary in either firmware image imports Reset_68013 via dynamic relocation (checked across every file in both trees). So the function exists and is semantically on-point, but its link to the DUML cmd_set=0x09/cmd_id=0x0f dispatch path could not be statically confirmed -- it may be reached only via a runtime-populated dispatch table (as seen elsewhere in this cmd_set's investigation) or may be dead/vestigial code. No aircraft-side decoder found despite exhaustive search. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: HDLnk Upgrade Tip Set
note: No Linux-userspace handler found. Checked the firmware-upgrade orchestration chain this project already catalogued (12_WM260_EXHAUSTIVE_BINARY_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md Sec.7 dji_upgrade; 20_FIRMWARE_UPDATE_PROCESS_FINDINGS.md's A/B-OTA tracks): dji_upgrade is a JSON-config-driven orchestrator (/system/etc/upgrade.json, fallback dji.json) that dlopen()s product-specific plugins and drives a fixed register_init/.../post_init sequence -- a config/orchestration client, not a DUML command registrar (consistent with doc12's own characterization). No register_dynamic_command site for cmd_set 0x09 exists in dji_upgrade or any libupgrade_*.so (none of those import duss_event_register_dynamic_command at all). The name plausibly means 'tell the HD-Link MCU an upgrade is about to happen, show a UI tip/LED pattern' rather than carrying actual firmware bytes, but no Linux-side code implementing that was found. No aircraft-side decoder found despite exhaustive search. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: HDLnk Max Video Bandwidth Set

name: Eye Push Target Pos Info
note: Checked this project's own docs first (21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md, 04/06/11/14_*.md) — no prior handler for this cmd_id. Independently re-dumped dji_flight's relocated dispatch table at vaddr 0xae038 byte-for-byte (confirmed 44 raw 8-byte rows through 0xae190, matching this project's prior count) and decoded its cmd_word packing (low byte of the 16-bit word = cmd_set, high byte = cmd_id; cross-validated against this project's own previously-confirmed cmd_set-0x22 rows 0x06/0x07/0x08/0x44, which decode correctly under this scheme). The table's only two cmd_set-0x0a rows are cmd_id 0xDD and 0xDE (vaddr 0xae188/0xae190) — 0x12 is not among them, ruling out dji_flight. Confirmed via `readelf -rW` on both dji_perception builds that neither imports any duss_event_register_dynamic_command-family symbol (re-confirms doc 04 independently). Resolved dji_perception E1E's real call sites to duss_mb_create_route_table/duss_event_create_client/duss_event_send/duss_event_send_sync via PLT-stub address arithmetic plus .ARM.exidx-anchored per-function disassembly (a naive linear Thumb sweep across this 20MB stripped binary desyncs after ~128KB and stops finding real calls — exidx-anchored per-function restart was needed for reliability). The real duss_event_send wrapper functions found (vaddr 0x63d0d8/0x63d268/0x63d428/0x63d728) build their packet entirely from a caller-supplied struct (a 16-bit cmd_word field at a fixed struct offset, plus payload ptr/len), so the literal cmd_id is set by a still-unidentified deeper caller. A literal-immediate scan for the packed cmd_word 0x120a found 2 hits in dji_perception E1E (vaddr 0x99e8da/0x99e8e4), but disassembling the surrounding code proved this is a rate-limited internal error/status-code logger (shared helper at vaddr 0x99e2cc, called identically from 3 unrelated functions elsewhere) whose internal module/error-tag namespace happens to also end in byte 0x0a — explicitly refuted as a DUML cmd_word, not a real handler. Searched the entire decrypted firmware tree (both E1E and E2 roots, every file, case-insensitive) for 'target_pos'/'push_target_pos'/'targetpos' — only hits are generic homing-planner/camera-tracking 'target_pos_x/y/z' fields (dji_flightsystem_msgs ROS-style schema strings), already characterized by doc 04 as perception-internal telemetry schema unrelated to DUML cmd_id dispatch (none of those string addresses is referenced by dispatch code). Reporting insufficient_evidence rather than a guessed layout. No aircraft-side decoder found despite exhaustive search. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

Dumping that table's id words (0xe00003, 0xe10003, 0xe20003, 0xe30003, 0xe40003, 0x400001, 0x410001, 0x420001, ...) shows sequential internal parameter-index values with no byte equal to the DUML cmd_set byte 0x0a anywhere in the pattern -- this looks like DJI's generic internal 'app_get_param'/'ss_get_param' parameter-store API (also attested by plaintext strings 'api_usr_get_param', '/device/terminal/0/request/app_get_param', 'TerminalRequestAppGetParam' in these binaries), not a binding keyed on DUML (cmd_set,cmd_id). name: Eye Get Buffer Config
note: Checked every known DUML registration mechanism on BOTH architectures and found no handler. (1) dji_flight's relocated .data dispatch table: re-derived it directly from raw bytes using the actual R_ARM_RELATIVE relocation offsets (44 relocations, stride 8, vaddr 0xae040..0xae198) rather than trusting the prior doc's byte alignment -- this corrects the row format to {cmd_word:u16 at row-4, cmd_set=byte0, cmd_id=byte1; fn_ptr:u32 reloc'd at row+0}. Decoded all 44 rows; exactly 2 are cmd_set 0x0a (cmd_id 0xDD, fn 0x1da05; cmd_id 0xDE, fn 0x1da55) -- neither is 0x48. Note dji_flight exists ONLY in the E1E (32-bit ARM) image; it is entirely absent from the E2 (aarch64) bin/ directory, so this check is necessarily E1E-only. (2) dji_sys literal duss_event_register_dynamic_command call sites: found via a capstone-based scanner that locates the PLT/import stub address and then brute-force decodes every 2-byte-aligned Thumb/A64 instruction in .text looking for bl/blx targeting it (not a text grep, which is unreliable on stripped ARM32). Found 11 call sites on E1E (vaddrs 0x2db80, 0x498ae, 0x4a23e, 0x4ac16, 0x4ac5c, 0x4be12, 0x4be58, 0x503a8, 0x504a8, 0x51ba2, 0x70064) and 12 on E2 (0x3ebd0, 0x62c00, 0x63790, 0x643a8, 0x6440c, 0x65690, 0x656f4, 0x68dd4, 0x68f70, 0x6cf9c, 0x96f58, 0x96f8c), decoded the preceding literal r1/r2 (cmd_set/cmd_id) operands at each: the full set resolves to cmd_set/cmd_id {0x22/0x60 x4, 0x00/0xa3 x2, 0x06/0x3a x2, 0x04/0x69 x1} plus 2-3 data-driven ('Param Manager') sites with no literal cmd_set/cmd_id -- identical on both architectures, confirming completeness. None is cmd_set 0x0a. (3) dji_perception: imports exactly ONE per-cmd registration primitive in either build -- duss_event_create_client -- and calls it from exactly ONE call site in its entire .text (E1E vaddr 0x63d98c, E2 vaddr 0xe2e3c), confirmed by the same brute-force BL/BLX-target scan. That single call site is reached only for JSON-config route entries whose 16-bit cmd_word passes two hard bound checks, confirmed instruction-identical on both architectures: high byte (cmd_set) < 0x20 (`cmp w1,#0x2000;b.hs reject` / `ldrh.w r1...;cmp.w r1,#0x2000;bhs reject`) AND low byte (cmd_id) < 0x42 (`and w8,w1,#0xfe;cmp w8,#0x42;b.hs reject` / `uxtb r0,r1;cmp r0,#0x42;bhs reject`), backing a compiled-in handler table only 66 slots wide per cmd_set (confirmed by the table stride, 0x210 bytes = 66*8). cmd_id 0x48 (72) exceeds this bound -- dji_perception's build cannot dispatch it via its own primary DUML entry point, regardless of JSON config content. (4) dji_sys also exports a batch-registration helper, duss_register_cmd (E2 vaddr 0x96ef0; this independently reproduces, exactly, a vaddr 0x6fff4 helper already flagged in this project's own commands.json note for an unrelated cmd_set-0x00 command on E1E) that walks an externally-supplied {cmd_set:u16,cmd_id:u16,...,handler:u64} array calling register_dynamic_command per row -- but a full .text BL/BLX-target scan of dji_sys found ZERO internal callers of it on either architecture, and no other binary in either firmware tree imports it either: it is dead code in this build, so it cannot be the actual route for 0x0a. (5) Every other binary across both e1e_extracted and e2_extracted trees that imports any register_dynamic_command/create_client-family symbol was enumerated and checked: dji_sdrs_agent (E1E, 1 data-driven call site, 'SDRS'-prefixed log/USB-diagnostic strings, unrelated to vision), test_rtos_raw (a dji_perception Parameter-Manager QA harness already documented by this project as covering only cmd_set 0x03/0x01), libMipiHandshake.so and libWorkModeLiveview.so (register literal cmd_set 0x09/cmd_id 0xaa, cmd_set 0x09/cmd_id 0xa9, cmd_set 0x02/cmd_id 0xec -- camera/MIPI pipeline, not vision), duml_googletest (E2 test harness, not inspected further as a production registrant). No handler for 0x48 found anywhere. No aircraft-side decoder found despite exhaustive search. See DUML_PROTOCOL/21_PAYLOAD_DECODE_SWEEP_FINDINGS.md for full search methodology.

name: Eye Enable SDK Func
