name: Upgrade/Downgrade Test Trigger
dissector_fn: binary RE: Sender: dji_mb_ctrl's getopt-driven CLI packs -s 18/-c 3d into the cmd word and the trailing hex string into the payload, calling duss_event_send_sync_v2 to device word 0x0806 (type 8/idx 6) -- independently re-confirmed in this pass (readelf -sW/-rW + disassembly) as already established in DUML_PROTOCOL/20_FIRMWARE_UPDATE_PROCESS_FINDINGS.md. Receiver: dji_lte's registered bus callback at vaddr 0xb5f0 gates on the destination word (ldrh [x21,#8] == 0x806) and calls a GENERIC frame-field logger at vaddr 0xb108 for every message addressed to that identity -- I disassembled both functions in full in this pass and independently confirmed, by direct inspection, that neither contains any branch on cmd_set/cmd_id anywhere, and neither calls any of dji_lte's own imported duss_event_resp_data / duss_event_resp_data_without_retcode / duss_event_resp_ok / duss_event_resp_err response-construction routines (grep-confirmed against the full disassembly listing). So there is no cmd-0x3D-specific handler logic to be found here beyond what the sender itself already establishes -- the name and byte layout describe the sender tool's intent, not a resolved receiver-side function, exactly as doc 20 already flagged.

Only these two literal values are ever observed in the firmware, both from dongle_upgrade_test.sh's own labelled invocations ('start upgrade' before the 0x01 line, 'start downgrade' before the 0x03 line). No receiver-side code was found that reads or branches on this byte specifically (see handler_function) -- its name/meaning is established from the sender's own intent, not from observed receiver logic.

No validation, length-check, or parsing of these bytes was found anywhere in the traced receiver-side code (the generic decoder at 0xb108 only reads the standard DUML header fields it logs, never anything past them). Reported honestly as filler of unconfirmed purpose -- it may be arbitrary pad chosen by the test script's author to fill a fixed-size buffer, or it may be consumed by logic this pass could not locate. fields.name: operation
fields.label: Operation / Sub-command
fields.desc: Dispatch byte read via ldrb at internal struct offset +0x14 (20) on both architecture builds. Selects one of three structurally different sub-layouts for the rest of the payload: operation=1 ('port switch') uses only byte1=switch_mode and replies synchronously via duss_event_resp_data_without_retcode with a 2-byte {return_command=1, return_code=0} ack; operation=2 ('route switch', detailed in the remaining fields below) is forwarded asynchronously to an internal queue with no immediate ack payload; operation=3 ('switch done') uses byte1=link_mode and byte2=type and replies synchronously with a 2-byte {return_command=3, return_code=0} ack. Any other value falls to a default branch logging 'RS: unsupport rs command :%#x' and returns an internal error code (-1001) with no wire response constructed at all.

fields.name: inverted
fields.label: Inverted flag (operation=2 only)
fields.desc: Named directly from this handler's own debug string 'RS: route switch: inverted = %d, old link mode = %d, new link mode = %d, type = %d'. Read via ldrb at struct offset +0x15 (21). Only meaningful when operation=2.

fields.name: old_link_mode
fields.label: Old Link Mode (operation=2 only)
fields.desc: Second value in the same debug string ('old link mode = %d'). Read via ldrb at struct offset +0x16 (22). Exact numeric encoding (e.g. which value means a wired vs. wireless transport) was not recovered -- only the field's existence, position, and name.

fields.name: new_link_mode
fields.label: New Link Mode (operation=2 only)
fields.desc: Third value in the same debug string ('new link mode = %d'). Read via ldrb at struct offset +0x17 (23). Numeric encoding not recovered.

fields.name: type
fields.label: Route/Link Type (operation=2 only)
fields.desc: Fourth value in the same debug string ('type = %d'). Read via ldrb at struct offset +0x18 (24). Semantic enumeration not recovered.

fields.name: host_id_count
fields.label: Host ID Count (operation=2 only)
fields.desc: Read via ldrb at struct offset +0x19 (25). Used directly both as the loop bound for, and to decide whether to execute, the host_id_list array below (confirmed on both architecture builds: a cmp/bls-style bound check against this exact byte gates the per-entry 'RS: route switch host id = %#x' log loop).

fields.name: host_id_list
fields.label: Host ID List (operation=2 only)
fields.type: uint16[] (little-endian, 2 bytes per element, repeated host_id_count times)
fields.desc: Array of little-endian 16-bit host IDs starting at struct offset +0x1a (26), each individually logged via 'RS: route switch host id = %#x'. 2-byte element stride independently confirmed on both builds: AArch64 indexes as `ldrh w4,[x28, x27, lsl #1]` with x28 = base+0x1a; ARM32 indexes identically as `ldrh.w r2,[ip, #26]` with ip = base + (index*2). Total field size is 2*host_id_count bytes; the size shown here (2) is for a single element.
